topicName: Selenium Grid Architecture (Hub-Node vs Distributed Mode)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Selenium Grid Architecture: Hub-Node vs Distributed Mode"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selenium Grid allows you to execute WebDriver tests on separate machines distributed across different environments, saving time and improving test execution scalability. Understanding the architectural differences between Hub-Node mode and Distributed mode is crucial for designing a robust test infrastructure."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Overview of Selenium Grid 4 Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"With Selenium Grid 4, the architecture was completely rewritten. Unlike older versions, Grid 4 separates the services into distinct components: Router, Distributor, Session Map, Node, and Event Bus. Depending on your scaling needs, these components can be deployed together in Hub-Node mode or separated completely in Distributed mode."},{"order":5,"type":"heading","text":"Hub-Node Mode (Classic Standalone Grid)"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"In Hub-Node mode, a single server acts as the Hub, combining all the core Grid roles (Router, Distributor, Session Map, and Event Bus), while one or more Nodes register themselves to this Hub. The Hub receives all test requests, determines the capabilities, and routes them to an available Node."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"How to Start Selenium Grid in Hub-Node Mode"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To start a Hub and a Node on a single machine or separate machines using Selenium 4, you can use the following commands:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar standalone"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Alternatively, to explicitly separate Hub and Node roles:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar hub
java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar node --hub http://<hub-ip>:4444"},{"order":12,"type":"heading","text":"Distributed Mode (Advanced Scalability)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Distributed mode breaks down the Hub into its individual architectural components. Each component runs as a separate process or container. This mode is designed for massive parallel execution environments like Kubernetes, where scaling individual bottlenecks (such as the Router or Distributor) is necessary."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Router: Receives external requests and forwards them to the correct component."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Distributor: Manages the registered nodes and decides where to create a new session."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Session Map: Stores the mapping between the session ID and the node hosting the session."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Event Bus: Acts as the nervous system, allowing internal Grid components to communicate asynchronously."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"How to Start Selenium Grid in Distributed Mode"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Running a distributed grid requires starting each component sequentially or via container orchestration configurations like Docker Compose. Below is the sequence to spin up components locally:"},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar event-bus
java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar sessionmap
java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar distributor --sessions http://localhost:5556 --bus http://localhost:5536
java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar router --sessions http://localhost:5556 --distributor http://localhost:5553 --bus http://localhost:5536
java -jar selenium-server-4.x.x.jar node --distributor http://localhost:5553 --bus http://localhost:5536"},{"order":21,"type":"heading","text":"Hub-Node vs Distributed Mode: Key Differences"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Setup Complexity: Hub-Node is straightforward and easy to set up. Distributed mode requires managing multiple services and network configs."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scalability: Hub-Node has a single point of failure and scaling limits. Distributed mode allows horizontal scaling of specific components independently."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Resource Utilization: Hub-Node consumes resources on a single Hub server. Distributed mode spreads resource loads across multiple machines or pods."},{"order":25,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choose Hub-Node mode if you have a small-to-medium test suite and require quick setup and minimal maintenance. Choose Distributed mode if you operate in enterprise-level CI/CD pipelines requiring high availability, fault tolerance, and cloud-native orchestration."}]
